The '''2019–20 Czech First League''', known as the '''[[Czech First League|Fortuna liga]]''' for sponsorship reasons, was the 27th season of the [[Czech Republic]]'s top-tier [[Association football|football]] league. The defending champions were [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]], who won their fifth Czech title in the [[2018–19 Czech First League|previous season]]. This season was the second one with a new league structure in which 16 clubs play each other home and away, until the league is split up in championship, Europa League and relegation groups.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfafotbal.cz/novy_herni_format/|title=Nový herní formát|trans-title=New season structure|work=Ligová fotbalová asociace|language=cs|access-date=16 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617165047/http://www.lfafotbal.cz/novy_herni_format/|archive-date=17 June 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Season events==
On 12 March, the League Football Association announced that all Fortuna liga games had been postponed for the foreseeable future due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="Coronavirus Postponement">{{cite web |title=LFA odkládá profesionální soutěže do odvolání |url=https://www.fortunaliga.cz/clanek/16008-lfa-odklada-profesionalni-souteze-do-odvolani |website=fortunaliga.cz |publisher=Fortuna Liga |access-date=13 March 2020 |language=cs |date=12 March 2020}}</ref>

After 2 months, on 12 May, the League Football Association announced that the Fortuna liga would resume on 25 May.<ref name="Football Resumes">{{cite web |title=Restart profesionálních soutěží schválen! Sezóna se znovu rozeběhne dohrávkou v Teplicích |url=https://www.fortunaliga.cz/clanek/16027-restart-profesionalnich-soutezi-schvalen-sezona-se-znovu-rozebehne-dohravkou-v-teplicich |website=fortunaliga.cz |publisher=Fortuna Liga |access-date=14 May 2020 |language=cs |date=12 May 2020}}</ref> The regular season concluded on 14 June 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/30-kolo-fortuna-liga-souhrn-vysledku-clanku-a-online-reportazi.A200612_121123_fotbal_min|title=Slavia se k výhře protrápila, Sparta je třetí a Příbram zase poslední|language=cs|work=idnes.cz|date=14 June 2020|access-date=23 July 2020}}</ref>

On 23 July, when the Champions group and the Europa League playoffs had already been finalized, [[SFC Opava]] - a team holding 15th place in the table had a suspected coronavirus case among their team members. The Czech League Football Association said it was not possible to complete the league's relegation group as a result of this, and the team was forced to quarantine. None of the three teams in danger of being relegated to the second league, namely Karviná, Opava and Příbram, would be relegated. From the Second League, the victorious Pardubice, and second-placed Zbrojovka Brno would advance to the first league, while third-placed Dukla Praha would not. The relegation group matches were suspended and no team was relegated.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://english.radio.cz/football-czech-season-ending-early-due-coronavirus-8687267|title = Football: Czech season ending early due to coronavirus|date = 23 July 2020}}</ref>

==Europa League play-offs==
Teams placed between 7th and 10th position will take part in the Europa league play-offs. The best of them will play against the fourth-placed or fifth-placed of the championship play-offs to determine the Europa League play-off winners. The winners will qualify for the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League#Second qualifying round|second qualifying round]] of the 2020–21 UEFA Europa League.

==Relegation group==
Points and goals were carried over in full from the regular season. The relegation group was scheduled to conclude on 7 July but due to three players from [[MFK Karviná]] testing positive for [[COVID-19]], the last two rounds of matches were postponed to 23 and 26 July.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/karvina-koronavirus-testy-negativni.A200715_205336_fotbal_rou?|title=Karvinští fotbalisté jsou zdraví, dohrání ligy nic nebrání|language=cs|work=idnes.cz|date=15 July 2020|access-date=16 July 2020}}</ref> Then, due to one player from [[SFC Opava]] testing positive for [[COVID-19]], the last two rounds of matches were not played. As a consequence, no team was relegated and number of teams for 2020–2021 season was increased from 16 to 18.
